- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially >3 consecutive negative values), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3 periods.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive downward moves), model tends to ignore trend; adjust forecast to align with 3-period moving average of true values.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model often overreacts to short-term volatility; smooth forecast by averaging with prior 3-period true value.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates true price in early periods (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% upward bias for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment history includes a recent negative spike (e.g., -0.33 or lower), model tends to lag in correction; add 1–2% lagged correction to forecast for next 2 periods.
